newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO sees only modest copper surplus ahead.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO sees only modest copper surplus ahead.

text.p: ASARCO chairman Richard De J Osborne said the copper market will remain in deficit this year and modest surpluses are seen for the next two years.
Osborne's forecast fly in the face of most industry analysts who expect hefty surpluses of metal from 1997 onwards as new mine production is cranked up.
At an analyst briefing, Osborne forecast a deficit of 78,000 tons in 1996, and a surplus of 63,000 tons next year, and 14,000 tons in 1998.
Problems at smelters and mines could see a shift to a significant deficit, Osborne cautioned.
Osborne noted that total copper stocks, including producer, consumer and exchanges, were down to 3.5 weeks of supply.
He added that he would not dismiss entirely that some inventory may be shifted around by "one or two big market participants to create uncertainty."

LME copper stock withdrawals at Hamburg and Rotterdam were being shipped to the Far East and could easily be part of "somebody else's effort to confuse the market..but I would not say all the withdrawals are for that," Osborne said.
Drawdowns from more regional warehouses such as in Italy, were likely for consumption, he added.
Osborne noted little metal was being delivered into LME warehouses. "All the new copper coming to the market is being taken by consumers."

ASARCO forecast that copper consumption will grow 3.1 percent this year, in 1997 and 1998. Asian consumption will grow 5.9 percent per year over the next two years, while Japan's will increase by 2.1 percent in 1997 and 1998.
Osborne said ASARCO's output this year, including production from its majority-owned Southern Peru Copper Corp, will be 1.011 billion pounds this year, or 453,592 tonnes.
Average ASARCO copper production cash costs were in the mid-60 cents per pound and Osborne saw no reason for this to alter significantly over the next two years.
